# Results — Study 770 (Concert-Economy)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**Live Nation (LYV) rallies INTO festival season**, front-running the summer touring
quarter in the weeks before Coachella opens the US festival calendar. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month). Fingerprint `4ba79257adcd`
(LYV + SPY, one combined panel, adjusted/total-return daily closes).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, `LYV` (Live Nation) + `SPY` (S&P 500), one combined panel: 5,161 rows, 2005-12-21 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: 20 Coachella editions 2006→2025 (2020 & 2021 COVID-cancelled → 18 held), weekend-1 Friday per year (Wikipedia per-year Coachella pages) |
| Events resolvable | of **20** editions, **18** have LYV+SPY coverage around the anchor (only the 2 cancelled years drop out — LYV IPO'd Dec-2005, so even 2006's 2-month run-up is covered) |
| Fundamental backdrop | **LABELLED PROXY** (10-K/10-Q reconstruction): revenue seasonality shares Q1 16% · Q2 28% · **Q3 37%** · Q4 19% — the summer touring quarter genuinely dominates the business |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the abnormal return (LYV − SPY) across independent, non-overlapping yearly events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); Wilson hit-rate interval; a 20-seed × 200-draw random-window placebo per cut |
| Execution / costs | **calendar-known, zero look-ahead**: Coachella's date is announced each January, so "buy K sessions before the weekend-1 Friday, sell as it opens" needs no surprise-day lag. Run-up = [anchor−K → anchor]; net of 2× one-way cost × NAV. Gross AND net reported |
| Price basis | **total-return** (dividends reinvested, `auto_adjust=True`) for both legs — labelled, not price-only |

**Beta, named on the Signal axis:** LYV is a **high-beta** name — its full-sample daily
beta to SPY is **1.35**. A raw `LYV − SPY` difference is therefore *not* a clean alpha:
over any long positive-drift window LYV will "outperform" SPY mechanically. This matters
only for the in-season window below (the run-up windows are short and the effect there
is flat regardless); it is the reason the one number that *looks* interesting isn't.

## The run-up — abnormal return, K sessions BEFORE Coachella (LYV − SPY)

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month run-up (k=21) | 18 | **+0.719%** | **+0.287** | 6/18 = 33.3% [16.3%, 56.3%] |
| 2-month run-up (k=42) | 18 | −0.527% | −0.182 | 8/18 = 44.4% [24.6%, 66.3%] |

Neither run-up cut is remotely significant. The 1-month "rally into" the festival is a
statistical zero (*t* = +0.29); stretch the window to two months and it turns *negative*
(*t* = −0.18). The hit rate is at or below a coin flip (6/18 up-years at 1 month). The
per-year 1-month run-ups swing wildly (from −14.5% in 2007 to +28.0% in 2009) with no
central tendency — the average is small because the years cancel, not because there's a
stable bump.

## Random-window placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws per event, right-tail)

| cut | observed mean | placebo mean (sd) | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month run-up | +0.719% | +0.882% (2.649%) | **0.518** |
| 2-month run-up | −0.527% | +1.668% (3.613%) | 0.729 |

A random K-session window on LYV vs SPY produces the observed run-up *more than half the
time* (p = 0.518 at 1 month). Note the placebo means are themselves **positive** (+0.9%,
+1.7%) — that is LYV's high-beta drift leaking in, and the observed run-up is *below* it.
There is no pre-festival signal to find.

## Robustness — jackknife on the 1-month run-up

Leave-one-out on the 18 events: full-sample *t* = **+0.287**; the jackknife range is
**[−0.435, +0.650]**. Every one of the 18 leave-one-out draws stays far below the *t* = 2
bar — no single lucky year is even *close* to carrying a signal, because there isn't one.

## Tradability — the run-up net of costs (calendar-known entry)

Because Coachella's date is public months ahead, the run-up window is fully tradable with
zero look-ahead; the only question is whether anything survives costs — and there is
nothing to survive.

| cut | gross | net @ 5 bps (*t*) | net @ 10 bps (*t*) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month | +0.719% (*t* = +0.29) | +0.619% (+0.25) | +0.519% (+0.21) |
| 2-month | −0.527% (*t* = −0.18) | −0.627% (−0.22) | −0.727% (−0.25) |

No cut clears **t ≥ 2** gross *or* net. Tradability = Mirage.

## Third axis — "front-runs the season?" (the in-season window)

The folklore's mechanism is that the stock *front-runs* the real Q3 revenue seasonality.
So we also measured the abnormal return from Coachella's Friday through the summer
(≈95 sessions, roughly to Labor Day):

| window | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| in-season (Coachella → ~Labor Day, k=95) | 18 | **+8.542%** | +1.912 | 12/18 = 66.7% |

This is the only sizeable number on the whole tape — and it points the **wrong way for
the claim**. The out-performance happens *during* the season, not *before* it; there is
no "rally into" and no "sell-the-news" reversal. And it is not real alpha:

- **Right-tail placebo:** observed +8.542% vs placebo mean **+3.359%** (sd 5.196%) →
  **p = 0.157**. A random 4.5-month window on LYV clears +8.5% about one time in six —
  the in-season number is inside the luck cloud, and the cloud is *centred well above
  zero* because LYV drifts up faster than SPY by construction.
- **Beta-adjusted:** replacing `LYV − SPY` with `LYV − 1.35·SPY` leaves +7.6% at
  *t* = 1.81 — still short of the bar, and the residual is generic high-beta drift over
  a long window, not a festival effect.

So the in-season move is **beta over a long horizon, not front-running of a revenue
event**. The mechanism the folklore names — the stock anticipating the summer quarter —
is **not supported**.

## Fundamental backdrop — the steelman is real, the front-running isn't

The revenue seasonality the folklore points to is genuine: in a normal year Q3 (summer
touring) is **~37%** of Live Nation's revenue vs ~16% in Q1 (LABELLED PROXY from the
10-Q filings). Festival season *is* a real business event. The finding is that this
well-known, entirely predictable seasonality is **not tradable through the stock in
advance** — exactly what an efficient market should do with a calendar everyone can see.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic paired (asset, benchmark) log-return world (ρ ≈ 0.6, like a single
high-beta name vs SPY) with a scheduled synthetic festival calendar and a TUNABLE
planted **pre-festival run-up bump**; no network.

| world | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (bump = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.20** (sd 1.07), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** |
| planted run-up = +1.0% (seed 770) | +1.07 |
| planted run-up = +2.0% (seed 770) | +1.89 |

The detector stays quiet on the null (1/20 seeds at |t| ≥ 2, the expected false-positive
rate) and its *t* climbs monotonically with the planted bump — the machinery recovers a
run-up when one is really there. On the real tape there is none to recover. *(A
faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The "rally into festival season" is a statistical zero: 1-month
  run-up AR **+0.719%**, *t* = **+0.287**, placebo *p* = **0.518**; the 2-month window is
  negative; the jackknife never approaches the bar. No pre-festival abnormal return
  exists.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Nothing to trade. The calendar-known run-up clears *t* ≥ 2
  neither gross nor net at 5 or 10 bps; the best case is *t* = +0.29.
- **"Front-runs the season?" — NOT SUPPORTED.** The revenue seasonality is real (Q3 ≈ 37%
  of revenue), but the stock does not anticipate it. The only large move is a +8.5%
  *in-season* drift that is (a) after the season starts, not before, (b) inside a random
  4.5-month window's luck cloud (*p* = 0.157), and (c) mostly LYV's 1.35 beta over a long
  horizon — beta, not front-running.
